title: Implementation notes: OB1 product completion
subtitle: OB1-W3 complete and merged; OB1-W4 is next · 2026-09-08 23:10 CDT
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change. Revert to flag for undo.

items.title: Ran W3 with the interactive orchestrator

body.Spec said: Run the ordered product-completion plan with documentation and verification gates.
body.What I did: Used this terminal as the coordinator and dispatched read-only specialists because the plan runner required model directives that the plan does not contain and rejected the approved dirty documentation state.
body.Why: The user explicitly requested this terminal as the orchestrator. The same documentation-first, review, test, and verification gates were retained.
body.Risk: Phase commits normally produced by the plan runner are absent. The coordinator owns one W3 diff and one final verification record instead.

items.title: Used a stable FTS identity map

body.Spec said: Add a result-ID-linked FTS5 table with same-transaction synchronization.
body.What I did: Used a contentful FTS5 table plus search_fts_identity, which assigns each public result ID a stable integer FTS row ID.
body.Why: SQLite can renumber an ordinary table's implicit rowid during VACUUM. An external-content design linked to that rowid could silently associate FTS text with the wrong result.
body.Risk: Title and body exist in both the public projection and the derived FTS table. Doctor verifies exact byte agreement and rebuild can replace the FTS copy.

items.title: Kept one shared FTS scoring corpus

body.Spec said: Apply allowed_space_ids inside SQL before ranking and LIMIT.
body.What I did: Denied rows cannot enter the rankable or renderable relation or consume a result slot. SQLite BM25 statistics still use the shared public-projection corpus.
body.Why: Per-space indexes or custom authorized-corpus scoring would isolate statistics but add storage, query, and multi-space semantics that W3 does not need.
body.Risk: Document frequency from denied public-projection rows can influence an allowed row's score. No denied title, body, identifier, or result is returned.

items.title: Derived a useful title for quick captures

body.Spec said: Weight title matches above body matches and prove that behavior in native smoke tests.
body.What I did: Quick captures use their first nonblank line, capped at 200 characters, as the source-search title. Other payloads fall back to the payload-family label when no line exists.
body.Why: The five-minute CLI has no title option. First-line titles make title ranking useful and testable without expanding the command surface.
body.Risk: Changing a quick capture's first line through a future import or edit path will change its derived display title after that path updates the projection.

items.title: Failed closed on stale projections and invalid provenance

body.Spec said: Project protected values before indexing and apply the same public boundary again to returned search fields.
body.What I did: Projection writes require a valid durable provenance shape whose source reference and durable origin agree. Fetch reprojects complete fields before clamping, and search omits a stale row when its complete stored fields differ from the current public projection.
body.Why: Projecting an FTS snippet or a 500-character fetch fragment can miss a protected literal cut at the fragment boundary. Trust also cannot safely come from malformed or unlinked provenance.
body.Risk: A stale row can temporarily reduce the number of returned search results until reconciliation or full re-derivation repairs it. It cannot reveal that the protected query matched.

items.title: Kept full projection re-derivation inside maintenance

body.Spec said: Make the live projection rebuildable from durable captures and canonical Markdown without exposing mutation through retrieval.
body.What I did: Added a private writer-lease-protected operation that validates all durable inputs first, then atomically replaces search documents, stable identities, and FTS rows. Read-only retrieval exposes no rebuild method.
body.Why: An FTS-only rebuild cannot repair text created under an older redaction rule. The maintenance boundary preserves the retrieval contract and gives a projection leak a complete recovery path.
body.Risk: The operation is intentionally not a default CLI command in W3. A future supported maintenance surface must preserve the same validation, lease, and all-or-nothing behavior.
